text:
maya: Quick sync request — telemetry team flagged a 3x spike in notify_ingest_bytes after last week's notify payload change. Thinking about pushing a compact payload (smaller field names + removed redundant metadata) to cut bytes. Anyone opposed to doing this as a pinned rollout?

alex: How compact? Do you have an example? Also, need backwards compatibility for Dedicated customers.

maya: example below — full vs compact. compact drops verbose keys and flattens a couple nested fields.

maya: ```
// full payload (current)
{
  "slo_id": "svc-123",
  "threshold": 0.995,
  "signal": { "p90": 0.997, "p99": 0.999 },
  "routes": [ { "team": "infra", "contact": "#oncall" } ],
  "meta": { "env": "prod", "client": "acme" }
}

// compact proposal
{"id":"svc-123","t":0.995,"s":{"90":0.997},"r":[["infra","#oncall"]],"m":"p:acme"}
```

sam: We already use the slo_id and route fingerprint in the console for grouping. Will compacting keys break UI grouping or attribution? The console expects certain keys from the notification schema today.

maya: Good call. Plan is: ingest layer accepts both schemas for 90 days; we emit a canonical_event after normalization so console/backends never see the compact form. That preserves grouping. The idea is to reduce bytes on the wire and the cost in the notify_ingest tier.

alex: If ingestion normalizes, then telemetry will still show the same tag counts, right? We need to ensure telemetry (notify_event_count, notify_ingest_bytes) keep a v1/v2 label so we can measure adoption. Add a metric notify_payload_version{v="compact|full"}.

maya: yes — will add metrics and a debug flag. Also want to gate compact by feature flag per-tenant so we can ramp.

ops-bot: [ALERT] notify_ingest_bytes increased to 3x baseline over 1h at 2026-03-21T10:12:00Z — triggered by route:tf-notify-ingest-prod.

taylor: From rollouts UX POV: console should show rollout status per-tenant with adoption % and telemetry delta. We don't have that UI component yet. Do we want a simple badge (rolling % adoption) or full chart?

sam: Simple badge + link to details is fine. Also add a hover that lists sample normalized fields so oncall can confirm grouping keys exist.

alex: API debate: do we version the notify endpoint (/v1/notify vs /v2/notify) or accept a header X-Notify-Payload:v2? Versioned path is clearer but more work for clients. Header is lower friction. Thoughts?

maya: Header approach preferred — easier for SDKs and proxies to flip. We'll still include a path version option for clients who want explicit separation.

taylor: UX checklist for rollout: 
- Console: tenant rollout badge, adoption %, sample bytes saved estimate
- Telemetry: notify_payload_version metric + notify_ingest_bytes delta per-tenant
- API: support X-Notify-Payload header, fallback to full schema when absent
- Ingest: normalization pipeline + warning logs for unknown keys
- Rollout policy: feature-flag per-tenant, 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 2 weeks

sam: Also add a noisy-alert suppression rule: when adoption toggles, we expect transient drop/spike in derived SLO metrics. Alerting should ignore <24h transient deltas during ramp. Otherwise we'll flood oncall.

maya: Agreed. Proposal: during the rollout window we set a temporary alert mute on the SLO-exposure-change rule if triggered by notify_payload_version churn. We'll annotate events in the timeline.

alex: One more: support library change — SDKs should be able to opt into compact automatically and fall back if server responds 415 or validation error. Add header X-Notify-Accept: compact to signal client preference.

maya: I'll draft the API doc and the ingest normalization spec. Will post a PR for the metric names and alert suppression rule. Can y'all review and we can schedule a 30m sync tomorrow?

sam: +1. Please include a sample of the normalized canonical_event shape so console folks can build the badge.

taylor: I'll scope the console card and mock a compact badge this afternoon.

alex: Thx — will draft the rollout playbook and the 24h suppression rule for alerts.

maya: Great — thanks everyone. I'll add the feature-flag ticket and link PRs here. :thumbsup:
